scenario: Satellite sensors detect glacier calving events only when the calved iceberg exceeds 2.0 km² in area. Observed mean area among detected events is 2.8 km² (σ=0.6 km²). Analysts wish to estimate the true mean calving size across all events.

data.description: Observed statistics among units exceeding reporting threshold

values.n_observed: only values above threshold are recorded

question: (a) Assuming the true distribution of calved area is normal with σ=0.6 km², solve for the true population mean μ such that E[X|X>2.0]=2.8. (b) What fraction of all events lie above the above 2.0 km² satellite-detection threshold threshold? (c) By how much does the observed mean overstate the true mean?

ground_truth.explanation: Solving the truncated-normal equation μ + σ·φ((t−μ)/σ)/Φ̄((t−μ)/σ) = 2.8 numerically gives μ≈2.64286. Only 85.8% of all events are actually observed; the observed mean overstates the true mean by ≈0.1571 km².

naive_answer: The true mean calved area is approximately 2.8 km² because that is what the data directly show.
naive_trap: The observed mean is a truncated-normal conditional expectation, not the population mean; it always exceeds the true mean for above-threshold samples.
reasoning_trace: (1) Let α=(t−μ)/σ. (2) E[X|X>t]=μ+σ·φ(α)/Φ̄(α). (3) Set equal to 2.8 and solve numerically for μ using brentq. (4) Solution: μ≈2.64286. (5) Fraction above threshold: Φ̄((2.0−2.64286)/σ)≈0.85801.
python_verification:
obs,sig,thresh = 2.8,0.6,2.0
def eq(mu):
    alpha=(thresh-mu)/sig
    return mu+sig*norm.pdf(alpha)/norm.sf(alpha)-obs
mu_sol=brentq(eq,thresh-20*sig,obs-1e-9,maxiter=200)
frac=norm.sf((thresh-mu_sol)/sig)
assert abs(mu_sol-2.64286)<0.005
assert abs(frac-0.85801)<0.005
assert mu_sol < obs
